Bozrah (of Moab)
BOZ-rah
proper noun
Hebrew Botsrah, “sheepfold” or “fortress”, from a root meaning to enclose or fortify; a city of the plain of Moab, distinct from the famous Bozrah of Edom.

📖 Biblical Definition

Bozrah of Moab was a fortified city of the Moabite plain, named among the towns brought under the prophet Jeremiah’s sweeping oracle of judgment: “And upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near” (Jer 48:24). It is to be distinguished from the more famous Bozrah of Edom, that red winepress of the LORD’s treading; this is the Moabite Bozrah, a stronghold beyond Jordan whose name, like Edom’s, means a fortress or an enclosed fold. Moab was the proud and settled nation, at ease from his youth, that had not been emptied from vessel to vessel, and therefore his taste remained in him and his scent was not changed. But the LORD had a controversy with the pride of Moab, and Jeremiah pronounced woe upon her cities far and near, that no fenced place should shelter her presumption. For “the LORD hath a controversy with the nations, he will plead with all flesh” (Jer 25:31), and before Him all nations are “counted…less than nothing, and vanity” (Isa 40:17). He shall famish the gods of the earth and be worshipped by men, every one from his place (Zep 2:11). Bozrah of Moab teaches that no wall is high enough and no fold strong enough to hide the pride of the nations from the judgment of God; every stronghold, far or near, must answer to Him.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A fortified city of Moab under Jeremiah’s judgment (Jer 48:24), distinct from Bozrah of Edom; a witness that no stronghold shelters the pride of the nations from the LORD.

expand to see more

BOZRAH of Moab, a fortress-city of the Moabite plain (Jer 48:24).

Distinct from the famous Bozrah of Edom, the winepress of the LORD.

Its name means “fortress” or “sheepfold”, an enclosed stronghold.

Numbered among the cities of Moab, “far or near”, marked for judgment.

A witness that no wall hides the pride of the nations from God.

📖 Key Scripture

Jer 48:24 — "And upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near."

Jer 25:31 — "A noise shall come even to the ends of the earth; for the LORD hath a controversy with the nations, he will plead with all flesh; he will give them that are wicked to the sword, saith the LORD."

Isa 40:17 — "All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity."

Zep 2:11 — "The LORD will be terrible unto them: for he will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A Moabite fortress-city under the prophet’s judgment; the entry recovers the humbling of national pride and the LORD’s controversy that reaches every stronghold, far or near.

expand to see more

Bozrah of Moab is a fenced city named in Jeremiah’s oracle, distinct from Edom’s Bozrah though sharing the name of a stronghold; the town itself provokes no modern quarrel.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that no fortress shelters the pride of the nations from the judgment of God. Moab was at ease, settled and presumptuous, and trusted in her fenced places; but the LORD has a controversy with the nations and pleads with all flesh, and He named the cities of Moab, far or near, for the sword. Before Him the proudest peoples are less than nothing, and He will famish the gods of the earth. Let the strongholds of men not be trusted, but the LORD alone feared.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Botsrah, “fortress” or “sheepfold”, from batsar, to enclose, cut off, or make inaccessible.

expand to see more

Bozrah — Hebrew Botsrah, “fortress, sheepfold” (Jer 48:24).

From the root batsar, to enclose, fortify, or make strong.

The same name borne by a chief city of Edom (Isa 63:1).

This Bozrah lay in the plain country of Moab.

Kindred to mibtsar, a fenced or fortified place.

Usage

"Bozrah of Moab was a fenced city of the plain beyond Jordan."

"It is not the Bozrah of Edom, but a Moabite stronghold."

"The LORD marked Bozrah among Moab’s cities, far or near, for judgment."
